essays.stem: Describe the main features of a smartphone or tablet, and explain how each one could be used in your work, in a workshop, on site or in a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: A smartphone or tablet has a touch screen, a camera, a phone and messaging, email, internet, and apps such as a calendar, maps, notes and a calculator. The camera can take photos of work as it is done, such as a finished weld, a fitted gate or a villa room made ready for guests, as evidence for a supervisor or customer. Calls and messages let me report problems and get instructions quickly. Email lets me send reports and photos. The calendar can hold job times and set reminders for site visits or guest arrivals. Maps with GPS give directions to a new job site or villa. The notes app can record measurements, guest requests or a list of materials, and the calculator helps with quick sums such as lengths or costs. Some workplaces also use apps for job sheets, time sheets or checklists.
markingPoints: Names the main features: touch screen, camera, calls and messages, email, internet, apps
Camera for photo evidence of work, with a trade example
Calls, messages and email for reporting and instructions
Calendar and maps for appointments, reminders and directions
Notes, calculator and work apps for measurements, lists and forms

essays.stem: Explain how to charge and look after a mobile device so that it stays safe and works well, including in hot, wet or dusty places.
essays.modelAnswer: I charge the device with a suitable charger and cable in good condition, on a hard surface where air can get to it, not on a bed or under a pillow. I do not leave it charging in direct sun or near heat, and I stop using it and report it if it gets very hot, smells of burning or the battery swells. I keep it in a strong case with a screen protector so that it is not damaged if dropped. In the Jamaican heat I keep it out of direct sun and never leave it on a car dashboard. I keep it away from water, such as sinks, showers and pools, and away from dust, sparks and spatter in the workshop, keeping it in a pocket or a locker. I clean the screen with a soft cloth as the maker advises, and I install updates when they are offered.
markingPoints: Suitable charger and cable, charged on a hard surface, not on bedding
Stops using and reports if very hot, burning smell or a swollen battery
Case and screen protector against drops
Kept out of heat, sun, water, dust, sparks and spatter
Cleans it correctly and keeps it updated

essays.stem: Explain the difference between Wi-Fi, mobile data and Bluetooth, and say when you would use each one at work.
essays.modelAnswer: Wi-Fi is a wireless connection to a local network and the internet through a router, such as the Centre's or a villa's network. It is usually fast and does not use up my mobile data, so I use it when I am on site at a place with Wi-Fi to send large files, such as many photos, or to install updates. I use only secure, trusted networks for work. Mobile data comes from the phone company's network through the SIM card. It works almost anywhere there is a signal, such as on a building site or on the road, but it costs money and uses my data plan, so I use it for messages, maps and small files when there is no Wi-Fi. Bluetooth is a short-range wireless link between devices close together, such as a phone and an earpiece, a speaker or a small printer. I use it for hands-free calls or to connect accessories.
markingPoints: Wi-Fi: local wireless network and internet through a router
Wi-Fi use: large files and updates, on trusted networks
Mobile data: phone network through the SIM, works almost anywhere, costs data
Mobile data use: messages, maps and small files away from Wi-Fi
Bluetooth: short-range link to nearby devices such as earpieces, speakers or printers

essays.stem: Describe how to take, label and send good photos as evidence of work you have done.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that I am allowed to take photos and that no people or private items, such as a guest's belongings, will be in the picture without permission. I make sure the area is safe and I am not standing near hot work or on a ladder. I clean the lens and check that there is good light, using the flash if needed. I take a wide photo to show where the work is, and close-up photos to show detail, holding the device steady and checking that each photo is sharp. Where size matters, I put a rule or tape measure in the photo. I take photos at each stage if asked, such as before, during and after. Then I label them, either by renaming the files or by writing a caption with the job, the place and the date. I send them to the right person through the agreed app or email, with a short message saying what they show.
markingPoints: Checks permission and keeps people and private items out of the photo
Takes photos safely, with a clean lens and good light
Wide and close-up shots, sharp, with a size reference where needed
Photos at each stage as required
Labels with job, place and date and sends through the agreed channel with a message

essays.stem: Describe how to keep a work mobile device and the information on it secure.
essays.modelAnswer: I set a screen lock, such as a PIN, pattern, fingerprint or face, and make it lock itself after a short time. I use strong passwords that are different for each account, and I never share them or write them where others can see them. I turn on two-step verification where it is offered, so that a code is needed as well as the password. I install updates for the system and apps when they come, because they fix security problems. I only install apps from the official app store and check the permissions they ask for. I do not click links or open attachments in unexpected messages, and I never give out codes sent to my phone. I avoid using public Wi-Fi for work accounts or banking. I keep the device with me or locked away, and I turn on backup and the setting that lets a lost device be found, locked or wiped.
markingPoints: Screen lock that locks automatically
Strong, separate passwords kept private; two-step verification
Installs updates and gets apps only from the official store, checking permissions
Avoids suspicious links, never shares codes, careful with public Wi-Fi
Keeps the device safe, with backup and find, lock or wipe turned on

essays.stem: Explain how to recognise and deal with scam messages and phone calls.
essays.modelAnswer: Scam messages and calls try to trick people into giving money, passwords, bank details or the codes sent to their phone. Warning signs include messages saying you have won a prize or a lottery you did not enter, threats that your account will be closed unless you act now, poor spelling, strange links, and requests for codes or payment. A caller may pretend to be from a bank, the phone company, a delivery service or even your boss. I do not click links, open attachments or reply. I never give out passwords, PINs or one-time codes, because a real bank will never ask for them. If I am not sure, I hang up and call the company back on a number I know is real, such as the one on their website or card. I delete or block the message, report it to my supervisor if it came to a work phone, and warn my co-workers.
markingPoints: Explains what scams try to get: money, passwords, bank details, codes
Gives warning signs: prizes, urgency or threats, poor spelling, odd links
Does not click, open or reply; never shares passwords, PINs or codes
Checks by calling back on a known, real number
Deletes or blocks, reports to the supervisor and warns others

essays.stem: Explain how to respect the privacy of customers, guests and co-workers when you use a mobile device at work.
essays.modelAnswer: I only take photos or videos that my job needs, and I always ask permission before a person is in a photo. In a villa or a customer's home I keep private things, such as passports, wallets, documents, children and family photos, out of my pictures, and I do not touch guests' belongings to move them. I never post work photos, customer addresses or guest details on my personal social media, and I do not share them in personal chat groups. I only send work information to people who need it, through the agreed work app or email. I keep the device locked so that others cannot see customer or guest information on it. I do not record conversations without permission. When a job is finished, I move work photos to the work folder and delete copies I no longer need, following the workplace's rules on data.
markingPoints: Takes only the photos needed and asks permission before photographing people
Keeps private items and belongings out of photos and does not touch them
Never posts work or guest information on personal social media
Shares only with those who need it, through work channels; keeps the device locked
Follows workplace rules for storing and deleting work data

essays.stem: Explain when and where you should not use a mobile device at work, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I should not use a phone while driving, because reading or typing takes my eyes and mind off the road; I pull over safely first or use a hands-free system only where the law allows. I should not use it while on a ladder, on a roof or at height, because I need both hands and my attention to stay safe. I should not use it while operating a grinder, welding machine or other power tool, or while walking through a busy workshop, because a moment's distraction can cause a serious injury. I keep it out of hot-work areas and away from water, where it can be damaged. In a guest's villa or a customer's home, and in meetings, I keep it on silent and do not take personal calls in front of guests. In all cases I follow the workplace's rules on phones.
markingPoints: Not while driving: pull over first
Not on ladders, roofs or at height
Not while using machines or tools, or walking through a busy workshop
Kept away from hot work and water
Silent and no personal calls with guests or in meetings; follow workplace rules

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would take if your device would not connect to Wi-Fi, an app kept freezing, or the storage was full.
essays.modelAnswer: If the device would not connect to Wi-Fi, I would first check that Wi-Fi is switched on and airplane mode is off. Then I would check that I had chosen the right network and typed the password correctly, and move closer to the router. I would turn Wi-Fi off and on again, or restart the device. If other devices could not connect either, I would report it to the person in charge of the network. If an app kept freezing, I would close it fully and open it again. If that did not work, I would restart the device and check for updates to the app and the system. If storage was full, I would back up my photos and videos, delete files and apps I no longer need, and clear old downloads. If I still could not fix a problem, I would report it to my supervisor or IT support rather than resetting the device myself.
markingPoints: Wi-Fi: checks Wi-Fi is on, airplane mode is off, right network and password
Wi-Fi: moves closer, turns it off and on, restarts; reports if others are affected
App: closes and reopens, restarts the device, checks for updates
Storage: backs up, then deletes unneeded files and apps
Reports problems they cannot fix instead of resetting the device

essays.stem: Explain why backups are important, and describe what you should do if a work device is lost or stolen.
essays.modelAnswer: A device can be dropped, damaged by water or heat, stolen or simply stop working. If its photos, contacts, job records and messages are not backed up, they are lost for good, and job evidence or customer details may be gone. A backup copies the files to cloud storage or a computer, so that they can be put back on a new device. I turn on automatic backup and check from time to time that it is working. If a work device is lost or stolen, I report it to my supervisor at once, because it may hold customer, guest or business information. The supervisor or I can use the find-my-device feature to see where it is, make it ring, lock it or erase it from another device. Passwords for work accounts should be changed. If it was stolen, it should be reported to the police, and the phone company may block the SIM.
markingPoints: Devices can be damaged, lost or stolen, losing evidence and records
Backup copies files to the cloud or a computer so they can be restored
Automatic backup turned on and checked
Lost or stolen: report at once; locate, lock or erase it
Change passwords; report theft to the police; block the SIM

practical1.title: Record, label and share job evidence using a mobile device
practical1.brief: As a group, use a Centre tablet or your own phones (with your permission and the assessor's) to record evidence of a simple task at the Centre. The assessor gives each member one item to record, for example a welding bench set up safely, a finished practice weld, a villa bedroom made ready for a guest, or a bathroom cleaned and stocked. Each member takes a wide photo and a close-up photo of their item, with a tape measure in the shot where size matters, writes a caption in the notes app (job, place, date and what the photo shows), and sends the photos with a short, professional message to the assessor through the work email or chat group the assessor sets up. Then each member sets a calendar reminder for a follow-up check. Take a screenshot at each step to show what you did. Help each other where needed, so that every member completes every step. Add the photos and screenshots to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A Centre tablet or phone for each member, or members' own phones with permission
The items to photograph, set up by the assessor
A tape measure or steel rule
A work email address or chat group set up by the assessor
photos: Each member's wide photo of their item
Each member's close-up photo, with a tape measure where size matters
Screenshot of the caption written in the notes app
Screenshot of the message and photos sent to the assessor
Screenshot of the calendar reminder that was set
The devices put away safely at the end, with any chargers unplugged
checklist: Checked that no people or private belongings were in the photos without permission
Took photos safely, away from hot work, water and walkways
Took clear, sharp, well-lit wide and close-up photos, with a size reference where needed
Wrote a caption giving the job, place, date and what the photo shows
Sent the photos to the right person with a short, professional message
Set a calendar reminder with the right date, time and title
Took a screenshot of each step
Helped others in the group and handled the device with care
safety: Do not use devices in the welding area while anyone is welding or grinding
Keep devices away from water, sinks and cleaning chemicals
Stand still and look around you before taking a photo; never take photos from a ladder
Take photos of people only with their permission, and do not photograph guests' or other people's belongings
Do not share any photo outside the work group set up by the assessor

practical2.title: Set up, secure and troubleshoot a mobile device
practical2.brief: Each member works on a Centre training device, or on their own phone if they agree and the assessor allows it. Step by step, and taking a screenshot of each step, each member: connects to the Centre's Wi-Fi (the screenshot must show the network name, never the password); checks that a screen lock is on (show the settings page only, never the PIN); checks for system updates; checks the permissions of one app and turns off one that the app does not need; checks that backup is turned on; and uses the map app to plan a route from the Centre to a job site or villa named by the assessor, then shares the route with the assessor. Then, as a group, fix three faults the assessor has set on one training device, such as airplane mode left on, Wi-Fi turned off and storage nearly full, explaining each fix to the assessor. Work in pairs or threes so that members can check each other's steps. Add the screenshots and photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A Centre training device for each member, or members' own phones with permission
The Centre's Wi-Fi network name and password, from the assessor
A training device with three faults set by the assessor
A job site or villa address from the assessor
Chargers and a fault record sheet
photos: Screenshot of the Wi-Fi connected, showing the network name only
Screenshot of the screen lock settings page (not the PIN)
Screenshot of the update check and of the backup setting
Screenshot of an app's permissions after one was turned off
Screenshot of the planned route and the message sharing it
Photos of the group fixing the three faults, with the completed fault record sheet
checklist: Connected to the correct Wi-Fi network without showing the password
Checked or set a screen lock and kept the PIN private
Checked for updates and checked that backup was on
Checked an app's permissions and turned off one that was not needed
Planned a route with the map app and shared it correctly
Helped find and fix the faults, and explained a fix in plain words
Took a clear screenshot of each step
Handled the devices and chargers carefully and left them tidy
safety: Never show or screenshot a password or PIN
Do not reset, erase or change any device setting beyond the steps in the brief
Use chargers that are in good condition, and keep cables out of walkways
Sit or stand still while using the device; do not walk about looking at the screen
